issues.body: Both `_NAME_RE` and `_KEY_RE` accept only the exact sequence prefix `- ` (`(?:- )?`). YAML permits additional separation spaces after a sequence dash, so a valid line such as `      -  name: Publish guard (#123)` is not matched and the truncated name passes the gate. The same limitation means a valid `-  run: |` header is not recognized as a block scalar, allowing embedded `name:` text in its body to be misclassified. The self-test covers only the single-space spelling, so it does not exercise this load-bearing lexical boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Accept one or more YAML separation spaces after the dash in both regexes (for example, `(?:-[ \t]+)?`, while retaining the existing indentation handling), and add self-tests proving that a multi-space `-  name: ... #123` is rejected and that a multi-space `-  run: |` body is skipped without swallowing the following sibling step.
issues.title: Valid sequence indentation bypasses the name-truncation gate

verdict.summary: The intended lint catches the repository's current instances and its included self-tests pass, but the source scanner does not cover valid YAML sequence syntax with more than one space after the dash. That leaves a straightforward false-negative in the load-bearing gate and can also break block-scalar suppression, so the claim that it enforces the rule on every workflow name is not yet supported.
